memory_update.text: AMKR is the cleanest US-listed direct OSAT/advanced-packaging candidate for the AI advanced packaging and HBM backend node; prioritize later verification of advanced packaging revenue mix, customer-backed capacity, utilization, and Arizona project economics.
FORM belongs in the underfollowed discovery lane as a HBM probe-card and test-subsystem supplier; key signal is record DRAM revenue tied to HBM plus advanced packaging/HPC test complexity.
COHU is a smaller second-order backend test and inspection candidate; HBM4 inspection, AI/HPC test-cell utilization, and HPC revenue outlook are the evidence hooks, but materiality must be verified.
TSM should be retained as the reference capacity anchor for CoWoS/SoIC/InFO and AI advanced packaging; do not let it dominate the underfollowed lane.

Non-US-listed OSATs and packaging specialists such as Powertech and ASE are important node comparables but excluded from this US-listed pass; later global passes should map them to validate whether US-listed names are true beneficiaries or just weaker proxies.

node: Advanced packaging, HBM backend, memory packaging/test, fan-out panel-level packaging, and OSAT capacity
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the AI advanced-packaging and HBM-backend capacity node. The two-lane list uses TSMC as the reference capacity anchor, then prioritizes underfollowed US-listed second-order beneficiaries: Amkor as the purest US-listed OSAT/advanced-packaging candidate, FormFactor as a probe-card and test-subsystem supplier tied to HBM and advanced packaging, and Cohu as a smaller test-handler, inspection, metrology, and HBM inspection equipment supplier. The node thesis remains a hypothesis: AI/HPC packaging complexity and HBM ramp intensity may create demand overflow, qualification bottlenecks, and higher utilization for packaging/test suppliers, but later layers must verify revenue mix, customer concentration, margin capture, and whether capacity additions dilute pricing power.
